title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-06-06

ai_review.summary: Good‑quality audience recording captures an epic ~46‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight with Elvin Bishop’s fiery guest stint.
ai_review.review: The tape delivers a historic June 6, 1969 show highlighted by a marathon Turn On Your Lovelight that stretches into the mid‑40‑minute range, plus standout moments from Smokestack Lightning and Beat It On Down The Line featuring Elvin Bishop on guitar. Sound quality is solid for a late‑60s audience source—clear enough to enjoy the jam while showing occasional unevenness and a suspected splice around 33:25. Overall the performance is praised for its raw, psychedelic energy despite Jerry Garcia’s late arrival and occasional lineup confusion.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for the show (especially Lovelight) across many reviews, with generally good but era‑appropriate recording quality; occasional criticisms do not outweigh the positives.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Decent clarity for a 1969 audience tape; listeners note solid mids and guitar presence, but mention uneven levels, a possible splice at ~33:25, and the usual vintage tape hiss.

standout_songs: Beat It On Down The Line
show_quality.setlist_flow: A single‑disc set dominated by an extended Lovelight that builds from tight riffing into a free‑form, psychedelic jam; guest guitarist Elvin Bishop adds blues‑heavy firepower throughout, while the rest of the band follows a looser, drug‑induced groove.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mixed notes – some say he arrives late or is absent on parts of Lovelight, others praise his tone when present.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentions being heavily dosed, bass sounding less driven; references commentary from his book about the night’s chaos.
